stem: Every option below involves gabapentin stock at an otherwise eligible Massachusetts hospital ADD. Which stocking actions are permitted under the current technician-stocking policy? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A nationally certified licensed technician uses the no-prior-pharmacist-verification Schedule VI shortcut for gabapentin.
A nationally certified licensed technician loads pharmacist-verified gabapentin under the ordinary supervised licensed-technician pathway.
A pharmacy technician trainee loads unverified gabapentin based only on a visual bottle check.
A pharmacy technician trainee loads pharmacist-verified gabapentin using required electronic validation under pharmacist direction and supervision.
A licensed non-trainee pharmacy technician loads pharmacist-verified gabapentin using electronic validation under pharmacist supervision.

explanation.core_reasoning: Gabapentin can be handled through the ordinary verified-stock technician pathways, but its PMP status excludes it from the nationally certified technician's narrow no-prior-verification Schedule VI shortcut.

choice_analysis.A: That narrow shortcut excludes PMP drugs such as gabapentin.
choice_analysis.B: National certification does not prevent use of the ordinary verified-stock pathway.
choice_analysis.C: The PTT pathway requires pharmacist-verified stock plus electronic validation.
choice_analysis.D: A PTT may load pharmacist-verified Schedule III-VI stock; gabapentin is Massachusetts Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.E: The licensed-technician pathway permits verified Schedule II-VI stock.

related_facts: Gabapentin remains Massachusetts Schedule VI while being PMP-reportable.
explanation.mpje_trap: Turning the gabapentin PMP exclusion into a blanket ban on all technician stocking.

reasoning_steps: Classify the technician credential and verification pathway
Apply the PMP exclusion only to the no-prior-verification shortcut
